description: Woody climber, young stems yellowish-tomentose, older stems glabrescent, longitudinally ridged. Leaves broadly triangular-ovate, 5–10 cm long and broad, margin usually broadly and shallowly crenate, base shallowly cordate or truncate, sometimes obtuse, apex apiculate, usually broadly rounded, or obtuse, sometimes acute; palmately 5-nerved, flower surface tomentose or softly pubescent; upper surface sparsely pubescent, papyraceous; petiole yellowish-tomentose, 3–7 cm. Inflorescences yellowish-tomentose, 2–4 cm long. Male flowers white or yellow with pedicels ca 1 mm; sepals 9, hairy outside; outer 3 narrow, minute ca 0.5 mm long; middle 3 oblanceolate; inner 3 obovate, all 1 mm long; petals 6, obcuneate, 0.5 mm long, glabrous; stamens 6, 0.75 mm long. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in male; staminodes 6, filamentous; carpels 0.5 mm long; stigma bifid, recurved. Drupes purple to black, glabrous; endocarp rotund in outline, 5 mm diam, dorsally bearing 2 rows of ca 15 pointed projections, each of which is linked by a ridge to a laterally pointing projection, the latter being arranged in 2 lateral rows.

description: Shrub or climber up to 20 m high; thorns axillary, recurved, up to 1 cm. Leaves lanceolate, attenuate at base, acuminate-obtuse or rounded at apex, 4–10 by 2–5 cm, ± velutinous on both sides, rarely subglabrous. Petioles 1–2.5 cm. Inflorescences corymbose, brownish hairy. Peduncles 1.5–3 cm; bracteoles 1–3(–4) oblong, ca 1 mm. Pedicel 1–1.5 mm. Flowers unisexuai, dioecious or polygamous. Male flowers densely grouped. Perianth infundibuliform, 3 mm long, obconical in bud, truncate at apex with 5 furrows; at anthesis limb 4 mm diam., with 5, larger recurved lobes, alternating with 5 shorter ones. Stamens 6–8, exserted up to 1 mm; anthers subglobose. Female flowers sometimes accompanying the male in a loose panicle. Perianth campanulate-urceolate, 2 by 1.2 mm, lobes not recurved during anthesis; staminodes not present. Ovary elongate; stigma fimbriate, often with 3 bifid branches, exserted 1–1.5 mm. Anthocarp club-shaped, 10–15 by 2.5 mm, puberulous, with 5 ribs each with a biseriate row of viscid glands, ca 1 mm long. Seeds 1, 9–11 by 2–2.5 mm.

description: Shrub or tree, up to 15 m (rarely higher); branches glabrous without thorns. Leaves opposite, ovate-lanceolate, slightly attenuate towards the base, acuminate-rounded at apex, 10–25 by 5–11 cm, glabrous. Petioles 1–4 cm. Inflorescences terminal, corymbose; peduncle 3.5–4 cm. Flowers bisexual or unisexua 1. Pedicels 1.5–6 mm with 1–3 small bracteoles. Perianth campanulate, 3–7 mm, 5-angled, slightly velutinous-papillose towards apex. Stamens (4–)6–14, unequal in length, exserted 2–3 mm; anthers subglobose, ca 1 mm. Ovary elongate; style with fimbriate stigma, exserted ca 1 mm. Anthocarp elongate, 2–4 cm long, with 5 viscid ribs; pedicel 1–1.5 cm.

description: Leaves elliptic, 6–16 by 2.5–5.5 cm, apex acuminate, base acute to obtuse; reticulation conspicuous and prominent on both surfaces, glabrous (rarely puberulous along midrib and main nerves on lower surface); petioles 0.8–2(–3) cm. Male flowers: sepals 9–12; outer ones minute, puberulous; inner 3–6 larger, rotund to broadly rotund, 1.25 by 1.25–1.75 mm, glabrous; petals 3, cuneiform, 0.5–0.75 mm long; stamens 6–12, 0.5 mm, shortly connate. description: Small liane or scandent shrub. Leaves elliptic-ovate to subovate, 11–16 by 4–6 cm, apex long and finely acuminate, base truncate, rounded or broadly cuneate; with 3–5 sub-basal nerves, lateral nerves prominent below, and strongly linking towards the margin, at least in distal half of lamina, puberulous below along midrib and main nerves, otherwise glabrous; petioles 3–6 cm. Male inflorescences axillary, several lax peduncied cymes per axil, 2–3 cm long, very slender, puberulous or subglabrous. Male flowers white, glabrous, on pedicels up to 3 mm or subsessile; sepals 6–9; outer ones smaller; innermost 3 elliptic to broadly elliptic, 3 mm long; petals 4–5, ovate, shortly clawed, 1.5 mm long; stamens 8–11, joined in a shortly stalked synandrium, 1.5 mm long. Female flowers and fruits unknown.

description: Liane with stem up to 10 cm diam. Leaves with petioles, 9–20 cm, pubescent, lamina broadly ovate to rotund, sometimes 3–7-lobed, up to half-way, 11–22 by 9–18 cm, base deeply cordate with sinus, sometimes very narrow, apex (also of any lobes) obtuse to acuminate and often mucronate, palmately 7-nerved at base with 2–3 pairs of distal lateral nerves, flower surface often glaucous and softly pubescent to subtomentellous, upper surface sparsely pubescent; thinly papyraceous. Inflorescences 12–33 cm long, flower lateral branches, up to 11 cm long; female inflorescences smaller and fewer-flowered, pubescent. Male fowers: pedicels ca 1 mm, pubescent, with 1–2 nanow bracteoles close to sepals; sepals 6, externally puberulous; outer 3 oblong to elliptic, 2–3 mm long; inner 3 broadly elliptic, 2–3 mm long; petals 6, fleshy, truncate, 1–1.5 mm long; stamens 2–3 mm long. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in male; staminodes 1 mm long; carpels 1 mm long. Drupes drying laterally compressed and irregularly rotund in outline, the raised lateral crests of the endocarp clearly visible under the pericarp, glabrous; endocarp semicircular-rotund, 5 mm diam.

description: Small climber without tubers; stems very slender, glabrous or papillose-puberulous. Leaves broadly triangular-ovate, to triangular-oblate, 3–6 by 4–6 cm, base truncate or very slightly cordate, apex obtuse or slightly emarginate, glabrous, flower surface papillose and sometimes glaucous; thinly papyraceous; petiole 2.5–7 cm. Inflorescence: axillary or on leafless stems, a tiny umbelliform, few-flowered cyme, ca 5 mm long, sometimes papillose-puberulous. Male flowers pedicellate; sepals greenish, 6, elliptic, 1.25–1.75 mm long; the inner 3 slightly broader, externally puberulous; petals blue-violet, 3, ± obovate, 0.75 mm long, with an inwardly projecting transverse fold; synandrium 0.75 mm long. Female flowers symmetrical; sepals 3(–4), ± elliptic, 0.75–1.25 mm long; petals 3, minute, ca 0.25 mm long; carpels 0.75 mm long. Drupes unknown.

description: Slender woody climber, up to ca 15 m, entirely glabrous, with subterranean fusiform tubers. Leaves lanceolate to broadly ovate, 6–17 by 2.5–10.5(–14) cm, base broadly rounded to cordate, apex usually attenuately acute or caudate, reticulation usually rather lax and not prominent, ± equally visible on both surfaces, papyraceous; petioles (2–)3–5(–10) cm. Male inflorescences usually axillary (sometimes borne on leafless parts of the stem) composed of several, peduncled, disciform capitula arising in the axils of persistent, triangular to linear bracts, 1–2 mm, along an axis usually less than 1 cm long, occasionally to 14 cm on old stems; capitula 3–6(–8) mm in diam., on filiform peduncles up to 20(–35) mm long. Male flowers sessile, yellow to green, very densely crowded on a disciform receptacle; sepals 2–3, ± oblong-elliptic, 0.5–0.75 mm long; petals 2–3, ± obovate, 0.25 mm long; synandrium 1 mm long, exserted. Female inflorescences as in male, but axis and peduncles thicker, especially at fruiting, also peduncles longer, up to 55 mm. Female flowers with very short pedicels, about 1 mm, sometimes partly united; sepals and petals as in male; carpels ± ovoid or ellipsoidal, ca 1 mm long. Drupas red, with slender pedicels, 5–10 mm; usually obovate in outline, (6–)8–11 mm long; endocarp perforate, dorsally bearing 4 rows of 10–14 capitate projections, divaricately lobed at their apices.

description: Slender climber, without a tuberous rootstock, entirely glabrous. Leaves broadly triangular-ovate, 12–17 by 9.5–16 cm, base truncate, apex broadly obtuse to acute, both surfaces with a very close fine raised reticulation, glaucous below; thinly papyraceous; petiole 10–13 cm. Male inflorescences an axillary umbelliform cyme, 4–7 cm long, 1–2 (? more) per axil. Male flowers on pedicels, 1–3 mm; sepals 6, yellowish, subequal, ± elliptic, 1.75–2 mm long; petals 3, oblate, 1 mm long, fleshy; synandrium 1.5 mm long, anther-ring very narrow. Female flowers unknown. Infructescences an axillary umbelliform cyme, ca 4 cm long. Drupes on pedicels, up to 4 mm, broadly obovate in outline, 6–6.5 by 5–5.5 mm; endocarp perforate with 4 dorsal rows of ca 10 thin transverse plates with entire margins, the plates of the outer 2 rows broader, the surface between the plates rough with irregular minor processes.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania crebra. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 321. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender climber, without tubers, entirely glabrous apart from any papillae. Leaves triangular-ovate, 6–10 by 4.5–7 cm, base usually truncate, apex finely acute, fine reticulation visible especially below; papyraceous; petiole 2–7 cm. Inflorescences axillary, a very slender umbelliform cyme, up to ca 2.5 cm long (to 7 cm in Himalayan specimens), reddish. Male flowers pedicellate; sepals violet or greenish-white, 6–8, ± obovate, 1.5 mm long, the inner 3 slightly broader, externally sometimes minutely papillose; petals 3–4, broadly obovate, 0.75 mm long; synandrium 1.5 mm long. Female flowers symmetrical; sepals and petals 3 (only very young flowers seen). Drupes obovate in outline; endocarp 6 mm long, with 2 dorsal rows of 7–8 irregular transverse ridges, the surface between them, ± papillose.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania elegans. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 320. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender climber with colourless sap, entirely glabrous, stems arising froma large exposed tuber; tubers of old plants interconnected; perennial stems, up to over 10 m long. Leaves mostly broadly ovate, margin often slightly lobed, 9–22(–25) by 9–22(–25) cm, base truncate to slightly cordate, apex usually, ± obtuse, flower surface minutely papillose, glaucous, with reticulation often drying pale, submembranous; petiole 6–25 cm. Male inflorescences an axillary umbelliform cyme, 3–12 cm long. Male flowers on pedicels, 2–3 mm; sepals 6, green or yellowish, narrowly obovate, 2–2.5 mm long, subequa 1; petals 3, orange, obdeltoid-obovate, 1–1.25 mm long, sometimes with 2 collateral inner swellings (± glands). Synanarium ca 1.5 mm long. Female inflorescence: much more condensed than the male, but attaining 17 cm long in fruit. Female flowers asymmetrical, on pedicels which elongate, 2.5–4 mm in fruit; sepal 1, elliptic, 1 mm long; petals 2, suborbicular, 1 mm long; carpels subovoid, 1 mm long. Drupes obovate in outline, 6 mm long; endocarp perforate, dorsally bearing 4 rows of 13–17 hooked projections.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania glabra. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 322. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Woody climber, entirely glabrous, growing from a flattish tuber near soil-surface; older stems with scattered pustular lenticels. Leaves broadly ovate with the margin slightly repand, 8–15 by 8–17 cm, base truncate to slightly cordate; apex obtuse to acute, flower surface with moderately fine reticulation; very thinly papyraceous; petioles 5–17 cm. Inflorescences axillary or from old stems, umbelliform cymes twice branched, 5–12 cm long. Male flowers on pedicels, 1–2 mm; sepals 6, green, unguiculate-obovate, 2–3 mm long, externally densely papillose-glandular towards the apex; petals 3, orange, broadly cuneate-obovate, 1.5 mm long, densely papillose-glandiilar within; synandrium 1.5 mm long. Female flowers (from Indian material) with sepal and 2 petals. Drupes obovate in out-line, 6 mm long; endocarp perforate, dorsally bearing 4 rows of ca 14–16 projections, hooked or broadened at their apices.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania glandulifera. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 318. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender climber, 2–10 m, without a tuberous rootstock; stern herbaceousor thinly woody, glabrous or crispately puberulous. Leaves broadly triangular-ovate to ovate, (4–)6–12(–17) by 4–10(–14) cm, base broadly rounded to slightly cordate; apex acutely acuminate to obtuse; fine reticulation usually visible on both surfaces, upper surface glabrous, flower surface crispately puberulous, ± papyraceous; petioles crispately puberulous, 3–12 cm. Male inflorescences an axillary compound umbelliform cyme 4–9 cm, bearing flowers in dense, subcapitate, cymose clusters, puberulous, usually 1–2 per axil. Male flowers green, white or yellow, sessile or subsessile; sepals 6 or 8, glabrous or puberulous outside, oblanceolate to spathulate, 0.75–1.25 mm; petals 3 or 4, glabrous, ± obdeltoid to suborbicular, 0.5–1 mm; synandrium 0.5–1 mm long, exsert or not. Female inflorescences similar to male. Female flowers with petals and sepals as in male; but number of sepals often reduced; carpels ± ovoid, 0.75–1 mm. Drupes red, sessile or subsessile (occasionally with pedicels, up to 2 mm long), ± obovate to suborbicular in outline, 4–8 by 4–6 mm endocarp usually perforate, dorsally bearing 2, longitudinal rows of about 8–10, transverse ridges which are often, ± 2-lobed thus forming 4 distinct rows of processes, ± papilliform in the 2 inner rows, broader and often hooked in the 2 outer rowsg surface between and around tubercles usually smooth, rarely rough.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania japonica discolor. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 315. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender climber, entirely glabrous, with small underground tuber. Leaves suborbicular to oblate, 5–13 by 5–15 cm, base rounded, apex usually very obtuse, sometimes abruptly acuminate, glaucous below with very lax reticulation, very thinly papyraceous; petiole 3–12 cm. Inflorescences of slender umbelliform cymes, 1.5–6 cm long, these either 1 to few and axillary, or racemosely arranged along an axillary shoot, the female more densely flowered than the male. Male flowers on pedicels, 1–2 mm; sepals 6, yellow-green, outer 3 obovate-oblanceolate, 1.5–2 mm long, inner 3 broader and abruptly narrowed to the base; petals 3, broadly obovate to oblate, ca 1 mm long; synandrium 1 mm long. Female flowers asymmetrical on pedccels elongating to 5 mm in fruit; sepals 1(–2) similar to male; petals 2 similar to male; carpels subovoid, 1 mm long. Drupes rotund in outline, 6–7 mm diam.; endocarp imperforate, dorsally bearing 2 rows of 11–12, transverse ridges slightly divided into a point towards the median line.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania oblata. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 321. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender woody climber, presence or absence of tubers unknown. Leaves broadly triangular-ovate, 10–12 by 8–11 cm, glabrous, base slightly emarginate, apex obtuse, flower surface glaucous and minutely papillose along the nerves, reticulation moderately fine; membranous; petiole 6–7 cm. Male inflorescences apparently on leafless branches, 1–4 compound lax umbellate cymes arising from a short shoot; the umbellate cymes, 10–23 cm long, with primary branches up to 11 cm long, papillose. Male flowers on pedicels, 3–4 mm; sepals 6, externally dorsally papillose, outer 3 narrow, spathulate, 3 mm long, inner 3 much broader, subobovate, narrowed to the base, 3 mm long; petals 3, fleshy, broadly elliptic with the lateral margins inflexed, 2 mm long; synandrium 2 mm long. Female flowers and fruits unknown.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania papillosa. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 322. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Erect herb, entirely glabrous, arising from a tuber, up to 8 (or more?) cm diam.; stems up to 30 cm high. Leaves mostly suborbicular, (2–)3–6 cm diam, sometimes mucronulate at the apex, reticulation rather lax on both surfaces, stiffly papyraceous; petiole 2–3.5 cm long. Male inflorescences: cymes axillary, ca 1 cm long, with slender peduncles, 7–8 mm long; or arising from the axils of reduced leaves along an axillary shoot to 5 cm long. Male flowers on pedicels 1–2 mm; sepals 4 or 5, yellow, fleshy usually unequal some joined up to half their length obovate, 1–2 mm long; petals 0; synandrium broad; sessile or on stalk to 0.5 mm. Female flowers unknown. Drupes suborbicular to subobovate in outline, 7–8 mm diam.; endocarp with a small central perforation dorsally bearing 4 rows of 16–19 curved, flattened, and ridged projections.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania pierrei . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 313. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Woody climber, without a tuberous rootstock. Leaves triangular-ovate, 7–13 by 5–10 cm, base truncate or broadly rounded, apex usually acute, reticulation very fine and raised especially below, glabrous, papyraceous; petioles 4–12 cm. Male inflorescences axillary, 1.5–2.5 cm long, an umbelliform cyme, or a few arising from a very short axis, glabrous or sparsely papiliose. Male flowers on pedicels 1.2–1.5 mm, in dense clusters; the buds papillose; sepals green, 6 elliptic to oblanceolate, 1–1.3 mm long, the inner 3 larger; petals 3, broadly obovate, the lateral margins inflexed, 0.5 mm long; synandrium 0.7–1 mm long. Female inflorescences similar to male but much larger. Infructescence axillary or on older leafless stems, 4–7 cm long. Female flowers subsessile; sepals and petals similar to male; carpels 1 mm long. Drupes yellow to red pedicels, 3–5 mm, sometimes sessile, obovate to suborbicular in outline, 7–9 by 7–8 mm; endocarp perforate with 4 dorsal rows of 9–11, thin transverse, ± plate-like projections irregularly divided at the apices, the surface between the projections very scabrid.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania reticulata. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 319. Accessed 2021-07-31

Craib in Fl. Siam. En. 1:69, 70. 1925) and S. pierrei (see above, p. 313).

description: Climber with very large tubers, growing above ground and often intercon-nected old woody stems, 1–2 cm or more diam., covered with a thick corky bark, young slender herbaceous stems drying striate, glabrous. Leaves broadly to very broadly ovate, base slightly cordate to truncate, apex very obtuse, 8–14 by 9–15 cm, minutely papillose on flower surface, and papillose-puberulous along the nerves and fine veins, upper surface sparsely papillose-puberulous, very thinly papyraceous; petioles puberulous to glabrescent, 5–17 cm. Male inflorescences axillary, subumbellate, 2–3 cm long, puberulous, the flowers in a subglobose cluster, 11–15 mm diam., the subumbels usually solitary, but sometimes 2–3 per axil, or racemosely arranged in a compound inflorescences. Male flowers on glabrous pedicels, 2–2.5 mm long; sepals greenish-yellow, glabrous or externally sparsely papillose, outer 3 oblanceolate, 2 mm long, inner 3 obovate to subelliptic, 2 mm long; petals 3, orange, glabrous, broadly rhomboid with lateral edges incurved, 1.25 mm long; synandrium slender, 1.25 mm long. Female inflorescences similar to male, flowering head 7–10 mm diam.; the subumbel solitary in leaf-axil, puberulous. Female flowers on pedicels, 1 mm long, asymmetrical, greenish; sepal 1, obovate, 1.5 mm long, glabrous or exter-nally papillose; petals 2, antisepalous, concave-rotund, 1 mm long, glabrous. Carpel 1, gibbous-ovoid, 1.5 mm long, glabrous; stigma divided into ca 5 short subulate lobes. Drupes glabrous, pericarp shining, drying close to endocarp; endocarp obovate in outline with a central perforation, 5–6 mm long, 5 mm broad, dorsally ornamented with 4 longitudinal rows of ca 17–19, short raised transverse ridges.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania suberosa. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 316. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender climber, entirely glabrous, ca 2 m high; root-system stoloniferous. Leaves subtriangular, 4–6 by 3.5–5 cm, base subtruncate and 3-nerved, apex acute, moderately fine reticulation prominent on both surfaces; petiole 2–3 cm inserted less than 2 mm from basal margin of lamina. Male inflorescence axillary, the subumbels 1 cm long, the branches (with flowers) only 2–3 mm long. Male flowers on pedicels ca 0.5 mm; sepals 6, whitish-yellow, elliptic-lanceolate, apex acute, scarcely 1 mm long; petals 3, oblate, 0.25 mm long; synandrium sessile. (From description of Chinese spms: female flowers with 3 sepals, broadly ovate, caudate, 1.5 mm long; petals similar to male; drupes red, broadly obovate in outline; endocarp 4.5–5.5 mm long, dorsally bearing 2 central rows of pointed projections, and 2 lateral rows of 7–9, transverse ribs, imperforate).
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania subpeltata. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 312. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender woody climber; presence or absence of tubers unknown; older stems with rather smooth pale fawn bark. Leaves broadly ovate to suborbicular, 7–9 by 7–9 cm, base truncate to slightly cordate, apex broadly obtuse, margin slightly and broadly sinuate; yellow-tomentellous below, glabrous and drying dark-brown above, thinly papyraceous; petiole 3–6 cm, puberulous. Inflorescences and flowers unknown. Infructescences borne few to several on short lateral shoots on older, leafless stems, subumbelliform cymes, 2.5–6 cm long, rather congested, glabrous; peduncles 2–4.5 cm. Drupes on pedicels to 3 mm, obovate in outline, 6.7 mm long; endocarp with a small perforation, dorsally bearing 2 lateral rows of ca 20 short transverse ridges, and 2 central rows of ca 20 adpressed teeth pointing inwards.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania tomentella. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 313. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender climber, containing red sap, entirely glabrous; leafy stems herbaceous, annual, arising from a large exposed tuber, up to 40 cm diam.; perennial stems less than 1 m long, up to 4 cm diam. Leaves broadly triangular-ovate, margin often slightly lobed, 6–11(–19) by 7–12(–20) cm, base truncate or slightly cordate, apex obtuse and mucronulate, flower surface minutely papillose glaucous, with reticulation usually drying reddish-brown; submembranous; petioles 5–15 cm. Male inflorescence: an axillary umbelliform cyme, 4–16(–21) cm long. Male flowers on pedicels, 1–2 mm; sepals 6, greenish, 2–2.5 mm long, usually unequal, outer 3 oblanceolate, inner 3 obovate, unguiculate; petals 3, orange, ob-deltoid-obovate, 1.25 mm long; synandrium 1–1.75 mm long. Female inflorescences much more condensed than the male, sometimes subcapitate. Female flowers very shortly pedicellate, asymmetrical; sepal 1, ± elliptic, 0.75 mm long; petals 2, ± suborbicular, 0.75 mm long; carpels subellipsoidal, 1.5 mm long. Drupes obovate in outline, 7 mm long, endocarp perforate, dorsally bearing 4 rows of 12–16(–20) subcapitate projections.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stephania venosa. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 317. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Woody climber; branches tomentose, soon glabrous, reddish-brown andshining. Leaves elliptic or oblong, (10.5–)16–19(–30.5) by 4–9 cm, coriaceous, shining above; base obtuse, rounded or subcordate; apex acuminate; nerves 6–11 pairs, prominent. Petiole 1.5–3 cm. Flowers yellowish, fragrant, in axillary racemes, 12–18 mm long. Bracts linear, 2–3 mm long, tomentose. Sepals. elliptic, 5 by 4 mm, obtuse, coriaceous. Stamens numerous; filaments, 4–6 mm. Gynophore 5–10 mm, hairy. Ovary 2 by 1 mm, glabrous; style short. Fruits 3.5 by 2.5 cm, woody, pale-orange when ripe; stipe 8–13 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Stixis suaveolens. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 260. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Stems puberulous to glabrous, striate. Leaves elliptic, lanceolate or some-times subovate, 6.5–11(–17) by 2–4(–8.5) cm, base cuneate to rounded (to subcordate), apex acute to obtuse, often acuminate, with 3–5, subpalmate basal nerves apart from 2–6 pairs of lateral nerves, main nerves tending to link up towards the margin, midrib on flower surface rugulose near the base, glabrous; stiffly papyraceous; petiole rugulose, 0.5–2 cm. Inflorescence: axillary or cauli-florous, pubescent, 2–8(–17) cm long; bearing 1–few-flowered, peduncled cymes, ca 0.5 cm long. Male flowers yellow; inner sepals broadly elliptic, 2 mm long, subglabrous; petals 3 or 6, cuneate, emarginate, 1 mm long, glabrous; stamens 3, clavate, 1.5–2 mm long. Female flowers: inner sepals orbicular, 2 mm long, externally puberulous; petals 6, oblong-elliptic, 1 mm long; carpels ca 8–9, less than 1 mm long, borne on short branches of a glabrous gynophore; stigma sessile. Drupes red, borne on a carpophore, 3–4 mm long, with branches 2–3 mm long, subcompressed, obovoid, 7–10 by 6–7 mm, glabrous; endocarp trans-versely and irregularly ridged.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Tiliacora triandra. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 346. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Large woody climber to 30 m; young stems conspicuously striate, ferrugineous-pubescent at first, later glabrescent. Leaves ovate to broadly ovate or elliptic, base truncate to cordate or obtuse, apex acuminate, 11–25(–29) by 4.5–20 cm, base 3–5-nerved with 2–3(–4) pairs of distal lateral nerves, glabrous above, puberulous to glabrous below, stiffly papyraceous; petioles 6–21 cm. Inflorescences arising several together from protuberances on old stems, racemose, (5–)8–28(–35) cm, usually ferrugineous-tomentose. Male flowers on puberulous pedicels, 2.5–5 mm; outer sepals 3, triangular-ovate to narrowly triangular, 1–2 mm long, lightly puberulous to glabrous; 6 main inner sepals white to yellow, elliptic, 4–5 mm long, reflexed at anthesis, glabrous or externally usually lightly puberulous; petals broadly elliptic, 2.5–3.5 mm long, erect and contiguous at anthesis, concave with lateral edges incurved, glabrous; stamens 2–2.5 mm, anthers either immersed in the thickened connective or rather prominent. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in male; staminodes linear-oblong, acute, 3 mm; carpels curved-ellipsoidal, 2 mm long; stigma shortly multi-lobed. Drupes at first green with white spots, later white to yellow (or orange), containing white latex, radiating from the discoid carpophore terminating pedicels 1–2 cm, drying ± compressed-ellipsoidal, glabrous, base narrowed into a short stalk; endocarp compressed, narrowly to broadly elliptic or subovate in outline, 2–3.5 by 1–2 cm, base rounded to obtuse, apex obtuse to sharply acute, surface obscurely to strongly rugose or rugulose.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Tinomiscium petiolare. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 304. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Allied to T. crispa, but differing by: Old stems, up to 6 cm diam. bearingscattered pustular lenticels, but lacking prominent tubercles. Leaves with a pair of hollow domatia, present in axils of basal nerves on flower surface. Flowers with 6 petals. Drupes yellow, radiating from a subglobose carpophore, 1 mm long, on peduncle, 5–7 mm; pericarp drying very thin; endocarp thinly bony, blackish-grey, 7–9 by 5–6 mm, broadly elliptic in outline, rounded at base, slightly keeled at apex, with a weak dorsal ridge, surface papillose or almost smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Tinospora baenzigeri. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 364. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Woody climber, up to ca 15 m, entirely glabrous; stems becoming veryprominently tuberculate, containing an exceedingly bitter milky sap, producing very long filiform aerial roots. Leaves broadly ovate to orbicular, 7–14(–25) by 6–12(–24) cm, base deeply to shallowly cordate, apex usually long-acuminate, very thinly papyraceous, domatia usually absent, although a flat pocket sometimes present in axil of basal nerves beneath; petiole 5–15(–30) cm. Inflorescences not appearing with the leaves, arising from the older leafless stems, often a few together, pseudo-racemose, very slender. Male inflorescences (5–)9–20 cm long, flowers in 1–3-flowered fascicles. Male flowers on filiform pedicels, 2–4 mm; sepals pale green; outer 3, ± ovate, thickened at base, 1–1.5 mm long; inner 3 obovate, unguiculate or acute at base, 3–4 mm long; petals 3, only the outer whorl usually developed (sometimes 1–3, reduced inner petals present), narrowly oblanceolate, flat, lacking papillae, 2 mm long; stamens 6, 2 mm long. Female inflorescences 2–6 cm, with flowers mostly arising singly along the axis. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in male; staminodes 6, subulate, scarcely 1 mm long; carpels 3, ellipsoidal, 2 mm long; stigma very shortly lobed. Infructescences (from Assam and Burma specimens) bearing lateral peduncles, 1.5–2 cm, terminating in a subpyramidal, 2–3 mm long, carpophore, below which usually persist reflexed ovate sepals, 2 mm long. Drupes orange, ellipsoidal, 2 cm long (when fresh); endocarp whitish, ± ellipsoidal, 11–13 by 7–9 mm, surface obscurely rugulose or almost smooth, with a conspicuous dorsal ridge and with a small elliptic ventral aperture; condyle deeply intrusive into seed-cavity.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Tinospora crispa. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 363. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Slender woody climber, up to ca 10 m high, entirely glabrous; stems up to 2 cm diam., prominently lenticellate, producing long filiform aerial roots. Leaves varying in shape, triangular, oblong, elliptic to broadly elliptic, ovate or obovate, 6.5–11.5 by 3.5–7.5 cm, base mostly truncate to slightly cordate, apex bluntly and shortly to acutely acuminate, reticulation raised on both surfaces, upper surface drying minutely papillose (due to large convex epidermal cells), often illdefined glandular patches present in axils of basal nerves beneath; papyraceous; petiole 2–6 cm. Inflorescences not appearing together with the leaves, arising from leafless stems; pseudoracemes very slender, 3–6 cm long; flowers in 1–3-flowered fascicles. Male flowers on pedicels, 1.25 mm; sepals deep green; outer 3, 0.5 mm long; inner 3, broadly elliptic, 1.5 mm long; petals 6, green, oblong-elliptic, flat, eglandular, 1.25 mm long; stamens 0.75 mm long. Female flowers and fruits unknown.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Tinospora siamensis. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 365. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Woody climber; stems puberulous when young, later glabrescent, with scattered lenticels and very prominent leaf-scars, developing a smooth chartaceous bark, producing very long, filiform aerial roots. Leaves ovate to subrotund, 7–15 by 4.5–12 cm, margin occasionally with a few broadly pointed lobes or broad1y sinuate; base deeply to only slightly cordate, apex acutely acuminate, tomcntellous or subtomentellous below, puberulous above, glandular patches sometimes visible in basal nerve-axils: thinly papyraceous; petiole 4–9(–12) cm long, puberulous. Inflorescences not usually appearing with the leaves. Male inflorescences solitary or few together arising from axils of protruding leaf-scars on older leafless stems, pseudoracemose, slender, 3–12 cm long, axis glabrous bearing few-flowered fascicles. Male flowers on slender pedicels, 2–5 mm; sepals yellowish or pale green, glabrous; outer 3 ovate, 1–1.5 mm long; inner 3, broadly elliptic, 3–4 mm long; petals 6, broadly spathulate to subrhomboid with lateral margins inflexed, 2–3 mm long, papillose externally towards narrowed base; stamens 6, clavate, 3–4 mm. Female inflorescences similar to male, up to 14 cm long, with flowers arising singly along the axis. Female flowers on pedicels, 3–10 mm; sepals as in male; petals 6, spathulate; staminodes 6, subulate, 0.75 mm long; carpels 3, ellipsoidal, 1.5–2 mm long with flat, lobed stigma. Drupes red, radiating from a 3-cornered, or shortly 3-branched car-pophore, 2–3 mm long, on a peduncle, 8–11(–15) mm; pericarp drying thin; endocarp bony, 7–9 by 6 mm, broadly elliptic to subrotund in outline, obtusely pointed at base, broadly keeled at apex, with a low dorsal median ridge, surface with irregular low tubercles, or irregular low longitudinal ridges, small elliptic aperture, ca 1 mm long, on ventral face leading to deeply intrusive condyle.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Tinospora sinensis. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 361. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Youngest parts white hairy. Leaves coriaceous, glabrous, sparsely hairy in young leaves, ovate or ovate-oblong, 7–12 by 3–5 cm; apex acute or acuminate; base rounded, sometimes oblique, with 2 basal glands; margin recurved; lateral nerves 4–7 pairs; petiole 1–2 cm long, sulcate, hairy above. Raceme terminal, 10–20 cm long; pedicels decussate, 1.5–3 cm long, articulate below the middle, flower portion persistent; bracts acute, 2–3 mm long, hairy on the back; bracteoles minute, ca 1 mm long, glabrous. Sepals triangular, apex obtuse, 3–4 by 2 mm. Petals yellow, slightly unequal, 1.5–2 cm long; limb 10–15 by 5–7. mm, oblong; apex obtuse; base truncate. Stamens: filaments broad at base, yellow, reddening, bright red after anthesis, 4–5 and 2–3 mm long; anthers 2–3 mm long, connective narrow, but distinct on dorsal side. Ovary 2–3 mm in diam. with a whorl of young wings on each carpel; style 6–8 mm long, glabrous. Mericarps sparsely white hairy, each carpel irregularly 8-winged, fine often larger than the others, 1–2 cm in diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Tristellateia australasiae. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 5. Part 3, 1991. Pg. 285. Accessed 2021-07-31
